what: How Python's tzdata and JavaScript's ICU name the same zone at the same instant, measured.
why: display_time_short/displayTimeShort is the one formatting in the port that cannot be made
exact: Python names the zone with tzdata's own abbreviation, JavaScript with ICU's, and ICU has
fewer. The rows where they agree are golden cases and the Python must reproduce them exactly.
The rows where they do not are THIS file, and both suites assert their own column — so a change
in ICU fails the TypeScript's test, a change in tzdata fails the Python's, and neither side can
be quietly 'fixed' to match the other without a row here failing first.
Hand-written and NOT generated, unlike testdata/golden/: no implementation can compute the
other language's column. Deliberately not a golden case either — the golden mechanism compares
exactly and has no tolerance by design (testdata/golden/README.md), and an 'expected to differ'
escape hatch inside it is precisely the hole that would hide a rounding divergence that matters.

rows.note: the owner's own zone: an offset either way, which is why the bot has never shown the difference
the market's zone, standard time; both libraries have the name
a 45-minute offset: both print +0545, which is what pins tzAbbreviation's four-digit spelling
winter: ICU has GMT, so this half of London agrees
summer: the same zone diverges, which is the sharpest case here — a zone is not agreeing or disagreeing, an INSTANT is
IST is also Irish and Israel Standard Time; the offset is the unambiguous one
CST collides with America/Chicago's; note the TypeScript prints the same +08 as Singapore
daylight time: both the name and the offset move
a negative half-hour offset, standard time
daylight time: -0230, the one case where the four-digit spelling and a minus meet
